newsitem.title: JAPAN: ANA says needs 750 bln yen capex over five years.
newsitem.headline: ANA says needs 750 bln yen capex over five years.

text.p: All Nippon Airways Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would need 750 billion yen in capital spending over the next five years to pay for new aircraft and parts.
Japan's second-largest air carrier also said it will add 53 new aircraft to its fleet in the three-year period which started on April 1.
It will also retire 25 aircraft in the period.
An ANA spokesman said that the 53 new aircraft had already been ordered.
The company has already announced orders for 41 of the aircraft, while it planned to exercise its option to order another 12 new aircraft, he said.
The company has not yet decided how many will be from Airbus Industrie and how many will be from Boeing Co, he said.
The airline is continuing its policy of fleet renewal to keep its aircraft young.
The company also said it expected operating profits to increase to 30 to 35 billion yen by 2001, although this would not be enough to cover its capital spending needs.
"We will have to borrow money. We would also like to think about equity financing," said Yoshiyuki Nakamachi, senior managing director, corporate planning.
ANA said it would pursue a further 20 percent reduction in personnel costs per seat kilometres through increased productivity.
Total staff numbers, including seconded and contract employees, are expected to grow 7.8 percent to 15,810 in fiscal 2001/02 from 14,660 in fiscal 1996/97.
Nakamachi also said that the company would increase staff related to the operation of aircraft, such as flight attendants, and decrease ground staff.
Over the same period, ANA expects operations to expand 45.8 percent in terms of available seat kilometres.
Asked about risks involving fuel costs and foreign exchange rates, Nakamachi said hedge and control risk was a major part of corporate strategy but he was not in a position to go into details.
Regarding ANA's China services, he said the company would like to improve its network to China, particularly to Shanghai and Beijing.
He said the company would like to double the number of flights to Beijing to 14 a week as soon as possible and could easily envisage tripling daily flights to Hong Kong.
ANA said key issues for its mid-term plan were the expected opening of a second runway at Tokyo's Narita Airport around 2000 and advances in Japan's bilateral air agreement with the United States.
A government source said on Monday that recent bilateral aviation talks had yielded a U.S. acceptance of more aviation rights for ANA, in line with other carriers covered by the current 1952 treaty.
Under the treaty ANA does not have as many rights to routes as other "incumbent" carriers -- UAL Corp's United Airlines, Northwest Airlines Corp and Japan Airlines Co Ltd.
